topic: Trait anxiety vs. anxiety responses — identity versus pattern
body:
**You are not an anxious person. You are a person whose nervous system learned to over-predict threat. Those are not the same thing.**

When anxiety is persistent enough, most people absorb it as identity. "I'm just an anxious person. This is who I am. I've always been like this."

The problem with that framing is that identity feels fixed. And if anxiety is who you are, there's nothing to work with.

But your nervous system is not your character. It is a prediction machine that has been trained — by experience, by environment, by patterns that were established long before you had any say in them — to flag certain categories of situation as likely threats.

Prediction machines can be retrained. Not quickly. Not without effort. But the mechanism that updates threat assessments is known, and it works in every nervous system regardless of how long the pattern has been running.

What doesn't work is trying to change your personality. What does work is systematically giving your system new data about the situations it has been misfiling.

You're not broken. You're running a learned pattern. And learned patterns have an entry point.

The guide in my bio is a good place to start.
